headline: Tariff refund boosts profit as full-year guidance rises
summary_short: Mettler-Toledo's Q2 FY2026 net sales rose 4.5% y/y to $1,027.3M and GAAP diluted EPS grew 18.3% y/y to $11.55, aided by a one-time $52M tariff refund; adjusted EPS of $11.46 rose 14% y/y as management raised FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $47.15-$47.50.
summary_long: Net sales rose 4.5% y/y (6% in local currency ex a one-time tariff refund) on stronger China and emerging-markets growth, with Asia/RoW up 12% and Americas down 3%. GAAP diluted EPS of $11.55 (+18.3% y/y) benefited from a one-time $52.4M tariff refund to cost of sales, partly offset by a $27.8M refund to customers that reduced net sales; adjusted EPS of $11.46 (+14% y/y) excludes both. Adjusted operating profit rose 9% y/y to $309.3M. Cash fell to $51.4M (-16.9% y/y) after $206.3M of buybacks; long-term debt declined to $2,044.7M. Management raised FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $47.15-$47.50 (from $46.30-$46.95) and sales-growth guidance to 4-5% (from ~4%); Q3 adjusted EPS is guided to $12.00-$12.15.

drivers.explanation: Sales grew on better-than-expected organic growth, including strong China and emerging-markets demand; local-currency sales rose 6% ex a one-time tariff refund. Americas fell 3% while Europe (+7%) and Asia/RoW (+12%) grew.

Gross margin rose to 63.3% from 59.0% a year earlier, lifted by a one-time $52.4M IEEPA tariff refund credited to cost of sales; the release does not separately quantify underlying (ex-refund) cost trends.
Adjusted operating profit rose 9% y/y to $309.3M on improved market conditions and benefits from the Spinnaker sales/marketing and productivity initiatives, alongside the organic sales growth.

Net earnings growth tracks earnings-before-tax growth (+16.4% y/y) less a slightly higher tax provision ($56.5M vs $46.3M); the release gives no cause beyond the revenue and one-time cost-of-sales items already noted.

Not explained in the release — EBITDA is not a management-discussed line item in this filing; its growth follows the same revenue and one-time tariff-refund dynamics noted for gross profit and operating income.

GAAP diluted EPS growth reflects the tariff-refund-boosted earnings above, plus a 2.8% y/y reduction in diluted share count from continued buybacks ($206.3M repurchased this quarter). Adjusted EPS (+14% y/y) excludes the one-time items.

Better-than-expected organic growth (especially China/emerging markets) and Spinnaker initiative benefits drove the quarter; GAAP figures were flattered by a net ~$24.6M one-time tariff benefit. Management raised both FY2026 sales-growth and Adjusted EPS guidance.
